function_diseases.function_description: The paraventricular nucleus (PVN) is a critical neuroendocrine control center within the hypothalamus, serving as the primary source of oxytocin and vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone) production. It plays a fundamental role in regulating the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis through corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) synthesis, which controls stress responses and cortisol release. The PVN integrates osmotic, cardiovascular, and thermal information to maintain homeostasis, managing water balance, blood pressure, and body temperature. Its magnocellular neurons project directly to the posterior pituitary, while its parvocellular neurons regulate anterior pituitary hormone release. Beyond neuroendocrine functions, the PVN influences autonomic nervous system outputs affecting heart rate, blood vessel tone, and immune responses. It receives extensive inputs from the brainstem and limbic system, allowing it to coordinate behavioral responses to stress and emotion. The PVN also participates in circadian rhythm regulation through connections with the suprachiasmatic nucleus. Oxytocin produced here mediates social bonding, maternal behavior, and trust-related functions. Damage or dysfunction of the PVN results in profound metabolic, endocrine, and behavioral disturbances.
function_diseases.disease_description: Diabetes insipidus (central/neurogenic), Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH), Adrenal insufficiency (secondary to PVN dysfunction), Hypogonadism, Hypothyroidism (secondary), Hyperthermia/Hypothermia (thermoregulation disorders), Anorexia nervosa, Bulimia nervosa, Obesity and metabolic syndrome, Stress-related disorders and anxiety, Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), Depression (related to HPA axis dysfunction), Autism spectrum disorder (oxytocin system involvement), Prader-Willi syndrome, Kallmann syndrome, Pituitary apoplexy (affecting PVN inputs), Hyperprolactinemia, Trauma or injury to the hypothalamus, Inflammatory conditions (hypothalitis)

function_diseases.function_description: The amygdala is a key structure for emotional processing, fear conditioning, and threat detection. It integrates sensory inputs and modulates emotional and autonomic responses. It is involved in memory consolidation for emotionally salient events and social cognition.
function_diseases.disease_description: Anxiety disorders, PTSD, depression, autism spectrum disorder, Kluver-Bucy syndrome, temporal lobe epilepsy, Urbach-Wiethe disease

function_diseases.function_description: The hippocampus is essential for formation of new episodic and declarative memories, spatial navigation, and context encoding. It is part of the limbic system and communicates with cortex and other subcortical structures.
function_diseases.disease_description: Alzheimer's disease, amnesia, temporal lobe epilepsy, depression, schizophrenia, stress-related memory impairment
